reviews.author: Nabanita Talukdar
reviews.text: I am writing about an incident at the Aberdeen branch on 12 October 2026 at approximately 20:10, while working as a part-time delivery driver. When I arrived, only two or three tables were occupied, yet the servers were gathered near the bar and I had to wait around 8–10 minutes just to get someone’s attention. When a server finally approached, I told him the order was ready and likely on the collection shelf. He checked the bag, insisted it was not the correct order, and walked away without properly resolving the issue. I tried to get another server’s attention, but he also initially ignored me. When he eventually came forward, he likewise claimed the bag was incorrect and appeared reluctant to check it properly. I had to insist that he verify the order number before he finally acknowledged that it was the correct bag. What disappointed me most was not simply the wasted time, but the lack of assistance, communication and professionalism throughout the interaction. Having several years of management experience myself, I understand that mistakes happen, but staff should be willing to check an order properly rather than dismissing a delivery driver who is simply trying to do their job. Delivery drivers’ time matters too, and we should not have to repeatedly chase staff for basic assistance or insist on a straightforward order-number check. I strongly encourage the management team to review this incident, including any available CCTV and order records, and address the staff conduct and collection procedures at this branch. I hope management takes this feedback seriously and ensures that delivery drivers are treated with the courtesy and professionalism they deserve.

reviews.author: kristina barkauskyte
reviews.text: Lovely Food, but Disappointing Customer Service Today, we visited Maki & Ramen with friends. This wasn’t our first visit, and there’s a reason we decided to come back! The food was absolutely lovely, as always, and the atmosphere was really nice too. Unfortunately, our experience took a disappointing turn when it came time to pay. When we approached the till and asked about our bill, the gentleman serving us already seemed visibly unhappy and irritated. However, things got even worse when we politely asked if we could pay separately. His reaction was completely unnecessary. He threw the card machine aside and looked at us as though we had asked for our food for free! We were honestly shocked by his attitude. Asking to split a bill is a perfectly normal request, and no customer should be made to feel uncomfortable or unwelcome for simply asking. Thankfully, another gentleman came over, and he was the complete opposite — very friendly, polite and happy to help us with exactly what we had asked for. We really appreciated his kindness and professionalism. Unfortunately, despite the delicious food and lovely atmosphere, the behaviour of the first staff member left a very unpleasant feeling and spoiled what had otherwise been a great visit. We genuinely enjoy coming to Maki & Ramen, which makes this experience even more disappointing. Good food brings customers in, but good customer service is what makes them want to return. Hopefully, this is something management will take seriously, as no customer deserves to be treated that way.

reviews.author: Maja Skowron
reviews.text: I am definitely biased in this review due to coming here whilst they have the £5 ramen deal, however I have tried to keep that in mind when assessing the quality for the price. I was here on a Thursday at 6.30pm and there was a large queue out the door, though it was moving relatively quickly. I had a reservation and was able to skip the queue so I’d recommend making one for this busy time (by 7.30pm when we left there was a small queue consisting of two(?) large groups). Despite how busy it was staff were still upbeat, and friendly (young, light-haired guy particularly), and we did not have to wait long for our food, or to be approached to order or pay; there was nothing i’d improve in terms of service here. I had the chicken ramen and my friend had the spicy (maybe ‘hell’?) ramen, both of which were very good and came in significant portions. I would suggest the chicken ramen over the spicy one because the chicken was very good and I felt the flavour of the broth was richer without the additional spice. I do think there are far too many noodles in comparison to broth and toppings which would be my main complaint for the usual price point (about £15 usually). However, I find this is the case in many manchester ramen spots so I wouldn’t say this would ruin the experience. Drink prices are reasonable, especially for soft drinks. The atmosphere is very nice despite how crowded it is, and I felt there was enough space between tables to feel comfortable and relax. If you have a seat against the window it provides you space to put down your bags/coats on the sofa-esque seating along the window. Overall, I would recommend this place for its speed, friendly service, nice atmosphere and tasty ramen which for manchester ramen is not unusually priced.

reviews.text: Vegans be ware! They served me real eggs. Maybe it was a bad day in the restaurant was busy so I’d like to give people grace. But me and my friend both ordered Vegan Ramen from the Vegan menu and even asked the waiter what was the best vegan Ramen there was? When our balls came, they both had egg in it. My friend wasn’t Vegan so I asked her to try the egg and bacon. She said the egg tasted a real egg and the bacon didn’t. I then asked the waiter if the egg was real and he said yes, I looked at him shocked I asked him for a vegan Ramen instead of apologising he asked me are you sure? As if I didn’t mention Vegan Ramen enough? As a Vegan there’s stereotype we always talk about us being Vegan and yes, that was me so I’m pretty sure I mentioned me being Vegan at least five times in the ordering interaction. There was no accountability or apology which is absolutely crazy. We asked for tapwater and that never came so I had to ask for that two times before it did. I get restaurants are busy and packed but Lets Be real this mistake is absolutely insane. So Vegan, if you’re gonna eat it be absolutely aware that you could be getting served real animal products which is a scary thought.

reviews.text: Went here for lunch with my friend and the wait time was incredibly long. We waited around 30 minutes for maki rolls and then, as a vegan, I was served a salmon roll and the server just left before I could say anything which was really frustrating. Then we waited even longer for the correct dish to be brought once the server came back. The food was really delicious once we got it but then we waited around 20 minutes waiting for the bill as well as being ignored multiple times. In the time, my friend was able to go to the nearby subway and back with cookies and i still hadn't been handed the bill. It was quite infuriating how a table next to us was offered a discount for a small error with a drinks order whilst the mixup with mine was treated with a brief sorry. Definitely put a damper on our day out. 😕

reviews.author: Sophia Khan
reviews.text: Unfortunately, this was a really disappointing experience. The sushi itself was okay, but nothing particularly memorable, and the overall standard of service and cleanliness let the evening down significantly. We waited around 30 minutes just to receive the bill, despite the restaurant not feeling especially busy. The service also felt quite unprofessional at times. We could see staff eating hand rolls during service, and the general presentation of the restaurant did not feel particularly polished. More importantly, our glasses were visibly smudged and some of the plates did not appear properly clean, which was quite off-putting in a sushi restaurant. The staff were friendly, which I do want to acknowledge, but unfortunately the service was very disorganised and the overall experience did not feel up to the standard I would expect for the price. I hope these are issues the restaurant can address, as there is definitely room for improvement.
